correctness.rationale: The unrestricted graph has three universal Rayleigh trace upper bounds determined only by cross and internal sums. The groupwise-uniform graph attains their minimum exactly. Piecewise-linear normalized cost has slopes changing at 2pq/(2pq-p-q) and 2p/(p-1) (p>q) or p/(p-1) (p=q). The equality conditions prove the stated uniqueness and critical segments, and strict quotient spectral separation yields nonuniform optimal high-price cross allocations. The standalone program successfully checked 3,055 cases/assertions including exact rational branch identities and independent full Laplacian eigenvalues.

originality.rationale: Inspected primary source texts give the general FMMP convex framework, unpriced complete graph and other topologies, and fixed-intralayer coupling problems, not the stated two-price universal phase theorem. Objective-implication comparisons separate effective resistance, discrete-time mixing and fixed-subgraph coupling. Risk remains that an unindexed explicit exact specialization exists.
residual_risks: Exact parametric results in unindexed matrix-optimization or mixing literature may exist.
Generic semidefinite or E-optimal design duality may be viewed as conceptually stronger, although it does not itself state or tabulate the exact thresholds and high-price optimal-face property.
The result does not fully classify nonsymmetric optimal allocations precisely at the upper critical price for unequal groups.

value.rationale: The result answers a structurally motivated all-size network design question with two explicit cost thresholds, shows when the optimal support changes from all edges to only one reinforced group to bipartite coupling, and proves the practically relevant loss of unique allocation at high internal price. The sharp formulas avoid repeated semidefinite optimization and distinguish continuous-time spectral gap from the related but non-equivalent resistance objective.
